excerpt: A complete guide to the hours and days after a South Carolina crash: the scene, the report, the insurer, and the deadlines that follow.
keyTakeaways: After a SC accident: call 911, document scene, do not admit fault. SC requires stopping (S.C. Code § 56-5-1210). 3-year SOL (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). Mandatory UM coverage (S.C. Code § 38-77-150). Comparative fault bars at 51%. Min insurance 25/50/25. Punitive capped at 3x or $500K (S.C. Code § 15-32-530).

faqs.question: What should I do immediately after a SC accident?
faqs.answer: Call 911, check injuries, exchange info, document scene, collect witnesses, do not admit fault. S.C. Code § 56-5-1210 requires stopping.

faqs.question: How long to file in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: 3 years from date of accident (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). One year longer than Georgia.

faqs.question: Does SC require UM coverage?
faqs.answer: Yes. S.C. Code § 38-77-150 mandates UM at same limits as liability. UIM must be offered.

faqs.question: What is SC comparative fault rule?
faqs.answer: Modified comparative fault with 51% bar. Slightly more favorable than GA 50% threshold.

faqs.question: What damages can I recover?
faqs.answer: Medical expenses, lost wages, pain and suffering, emotional distress, property damage, loss of enjoyment. Punitive capped at 3x or $500K (S.C. Code § 15-32-530).

faqs.question: When to hire a lawyer?
faqs.answer: As soon as possible. Roden Law has offices in Charleston, Columbia, and Myrtle Beach. Free consultation.
